confirmed.claim: The driving-line API snapshot caches vTop() and is only refreshed when the track OBJECT changes, so changing OVERALL SPEED leaves the racing line's speed model — and the audible brake cue — pinned to the old pace.
confirmed.evidence: game.js:3020-3030 `function drivingLineApi(trk) { if (_dlApi.track !== trk) { ... _dlApi.vTop = vTop(); _dlApi.grip = 1; } return _dlApi; }`. js/render/shared/driving-line.js:220 `if (cache.id !== api.id || !cache.verts) build(api);` and :133/:141 `const vTop = api.vTop || 72 ... v[i] = Math.min(vTop, Math.sqrt(latMax*grip/k));` — the cache key is the circuit id only. G.PACE's setter (game.js:2660) does `PACE = v; GameCams.init(...)` and touches neither. js/input/steer-tuning.js:515-517 wires the live pause-menu slider `$("pm-pace").oninput = ... G.PACE = paceFromSlider(v)`. game.js:3491 feeds the brake beep from `DrivingLine.cue(Math.abs(player.speed), player.s)`, which reads that same stale LUT. Trigger: start a race, open the pause menu, move OVERALL SPEED — the ribbon's braking-zone colours and the brake beep now compare real speed against a line speed built for the previous vTop (cue silent when pace is lowered, permanently firing when raised). loadTrack's rebuild gate (game.js:2000) keeps the same `track` object across restarts on the same circuit, so the staleness also survives a race restart.
confirmed.fix: Refresh `_dlApi.vTop`/`grip` on every call and include vTop in DrivingLine's cache key (e.g. `cache.id !== api.id || cache.vTop !== api.vTop`) so the LUT rebuilds on a pace change.

confirmed.claim: The amber mirror-lamp speed gate applies vStd() to the constant instead of to the speed, inverting the PACE scaling it claims to add.

Every other site in the file normalises the speed instead (e.g. 4750 `vStd(c.speed) > 30`, 7156 `vStd(c.speed) > 15`); the correct form here is `vStd(c.speed) < 5.56`, i.e. `c.speed < 5.56 * PACE`. tools/check/vstd-lint.mjs only flags speed-vs-literal comparisons, so this form passes it.

confirmed.claim: The brake cue's lookahead is clamped to a bare 120 metres written on the PACE-1 speed scale, so with OVERALL SPEED above ~1 the cue fires long after the correct braking point.
confirmed.evidence: Line 60: `const look = clamp(Math.abs(p.speed) * cfg.lookSec, 28, 120);` — a raw metre clamp, then lines 63-69 sample only within `look`. Braking deceleration is absolute (js/game.js:2843-2846 "LAT_MAX and BRAKE are absolute in the driving model … not pace-scaled", PhysicsConsts.BRAKE = 22) while top speed is `vTop() = VMAX * PACE` (js/game.js:519), so braking distance grows with PACE². Concrete trigger: OVERALL SPEED 2 (PACE 2, vTop 144 m/s), player at 140 m/s approaching a 400 m-radius corner — vC = sqrt(22·400) = 94 m/s, so the ideal braking point is (140²−94²)/(2·22) ≈ 245 m out, but urgencyOf is never evaluated further than 120 m ahead. Even at PACE 1 the cap binds: 72 m/s × the notch-10 lookSec of 2.3 s = 165 m, so the top notches of the slider are indistinguishable.
confirmed.fix: Scale the clamp bounds by the speed envelope (e.g. `clamp(|p.speed|*cfg.lookSec, 28*PACE, 120*PACE)` via a G-supplied vTop()/VMAX factor) instead of bare metres.

confirmed.claim: Under spatial upscale the headless soft-present reads a render-size FBO with present-size dimensions, so the captured overlay is the scene in the bottom-left corner surrounded by undefined/black pixels.
confirmed.evidence: post.js:966-967 sets `_softReadFB = (useFxaa && aaFBO) ? aaFBO : ldrFBO` on the `useUpscale` path; aaTex (post.js:432) and ldrTex (post.js:408) are both allocated at createTargets' `width,height`, i.e. RENDER size, and wantSpatialUpscale() requires renderScale < 0.98 (glx.js:935). glx.js softBlit reads `const w = (gl.drawingBufferWidth|0) || (width|0)` / same for h (glx.js:466-467), and resize() sets canvas.width/height to presentW/presentH when `up` is true (glx.js:1034-1039). readbackLdrPixels then does `gl.readPixels(0,0,w,h,...)` against `_softReadFB` (post.js:1000-1001) — a present-size rect out of a render-size framebuffer. The comment at glx.js:462-465 explains drawingBuffer size was chosen because the read target was assumed to be the present-size DEFAULT framebuffer; post.js's upscale branch reads a pre-SGSR buffer instead, so the two fixes now contradict each other.
confirmed.fix: In softBlit use the post chain's actual read-buffer size (add a size getter next to postPath()/readbackLdrPixels) instead of gl.drawingBufferWidth/Height, or set `_softReadFB = null` on the useUpscale path so the present-size default FB is read.

confirmed.claim: The `else if (toLdr)` arm of the soft-read-FB selection is unreachable given how `toLdr` is defined.

The same function in js/render/glx/glx.js:2043-2046 writes `const idx = cs[ks[ci]].idx; for (let j = 0, jn = idx.length; j < jn; j++) { const i = idx[j];`. The shadow path always misses both caches (line 5321 `const shadow = ...upload === false`, line 5322 `let samePack = !shadow && ...`, line 5347 `if (!shadow && res && ...)`), and js/render/shared/shadow-pass.js:88 calls it once per prop batch on the per-frame lamp shadow pass, so the allocation recurs every frame for every visible cell of every batch.

confirmed.claim: `_litPipeline` builds a fresh 7-part concatenated string key on every draw/drawChunked/drawInstanced call purely to look up an already-cached pipeline.
confirmed.evidence: Lines 1950-1952: `const key = (blend ? 1 : 0) + "|" + (dbl ? 1 : 0) + "|" + (noAW ? 1 : 0) + "|" + samples + "|" + dbC + "|" + dbS + "|" + (decal ? 1 : 0); let p = _litPipelines.get(key); if (p) return p;` — the early return is after the string is built. It is called once per `draw` (3838), once per `drawChunked` (3860) and once per `drawInstanced` (5429); the file's own comment at 3741-3742 measures "~320 draws" in a Monza race frame, so this is ~320 short-string allocations plus string hashing every frame. This is the same per-frame GC class the file already pooled away for `_litOptsBag` (3796), `_mrRun` (4067) and `_instDrawOpts` (1022). `litPipelineStats` (6184) reports the variant count saturates at 9, so the string is discarded essentially every time.
confirmed.fix: Key the cache on a collision-free integer (e.g. nested Maps on `dbC`/`dbS`, or pack the flags with the two biases stored in separate Map levels) so the hot path allocates nothing.

confirmed.claim: On the three-WebGPU path the post chain is handed a WebGPU-convention inverse projection while tsl-post still converts depth with `d*2-1`, so every SSAO and SSR view-space position is reconstructed at roughly half its true depth.
confirmed.evidence: tlx.js:2937-2938 `_mul4Col(_invProjGpu, frame.invProj, Z01INV); _postF.invProj = _invProjGpu;` — `_mul4Col(out,a,b)` is a*b (same helper builds `_projGpu = Z01*proj` at 2919), so `_invProjGpu = inv(Z01·P)`, i.e. it already expects raw NDC z in [0,1]. tsl-post.js:171-175 `ssaoViewPosFromD = (uvGl,d) => { const c = vec4(uvGl.mul(2).sub(1), d.mul(2).sub(1), 1.0); const v = ssaoU.invProj.mul(c); ...}` and the identical `ssrViewPos` at tsl-post.js:455-459 both apply the GL remap `d*2-1` first. I reproduced the arithmetic numerically with a 60°/0.3/4000 GL projection and a view point (3,-1.5,-40): shader-as-written with `_invProjGpu` returns (1.508,-0.754,-20.101); with the unremapped `frame.invProj` it returns (3,-1.5,-40) exactly. The sibling matrix confirms the intent — `_postF.invVP` (tlx.js:2942) is left in GL convention and the godray march that consumes it (tsl-post.js `worldPos`) uses the same `d*2-1`, and is therefore correct.
confirmed.fix: On the `_wgpu` branch leave `_postF.invProj = frame.invProj` (the GL-convention matrix the shaders' `d*2-1` expects), as is already done for `_postF.invVP`.

confirmed.claim: The shared decal node graph bakes the FIRST non-zero `glow` value it is ever built with, so every later decal with a different glow renders at the wrong emissive lift.
confirmed.evidence: tsl-fx.js:208-227 `sharedDecal(glow)` buckets on `const gi = glow ? 1 : 0` and caches one graph per bucket in `_decalGraph`, while the graph body closes over the raw JS number: `const rgb = t.rgb.mul(amb.add(...)).add(t.rgb.mul(glow));`. `decalMaterialFor` (tsl-fx.js:229-260) keys its material cache on `tex.id + "|" + glow` so distinct glow values get distinct materials, but all of them call `sharedDecal(glow)` and get the same baked constant. The callers pass several distinct non-zero values: js/garage/scene.js:1110 `LIVE_OPTS = { glow: 0.62 }` and :1256 `DRESS_OPTS = { glow: 0.62 }`, js/car/car-draw.js:277 `_decalOpts.glow = night ? 0.35 : 0`. Visiting the garage first (0.62) then racing at night therefore lifts car sponsor decals by 0.62 instead of 0.35; the reverse order under-lifts the garage wall decals. GLX passes uGlow as a per-draw uniform (js/render/glx/glx.js drawDecal), so this is a TLX-only parity break.
confirmed.fix: Make glow a `uniform()` set per draw in `decalMaterialFor` (one node, `.value = glow`) instead of a JS constant closed over by the cached graph.

confirmed.claim: The peer-supplied `d.at` on an EV.START event is never validated, so a non-numeric or absurd value wedges the guest on the grid permanently — the exact hang the adjacent comment guards `d.hold` against.
confirmed.evidence: netplay.js:359-362 reads `if (name === EV.START && d && d.at != null && !ownsRaceControl()) { const h = Number(d.hold); armStart(d.at, Number.isFinite(h) ? Math.min(2, Math.max(0, h)) : 0.5); }` — `hold` is coerced and range-clamped, `at` is only checked for `!= null`. armStart (netplay.js:552-555) does `session.peerToLocal(atPeerMs)` (a subtraction) and stores `G.netStart = {at, hold, now}`. game.js:3338-3340 then computes `countT = (COUNTDOWN_S + startHold) - (netStart.at - netStart.now()) / 1000`; with at = NaN (e.g. `{at:"x"}` or `{at:{}}`) countT is NaN, so `lit = Math.min(COUNTDOWN_S, Math.floor(countT))` is NaN, `lit > lightsLit` is false (no lamps ever light) and `countT > COUNTDOWN_S + startHold` (game.js:3378) is false forever. A finite but absurd `at` (1e15) does the same with a huge negative countT. The HOLD_MAX_MS backstop cannot save it: netplay.js:744 `awaitingStart` requires `!G.netStart`, and netStart is now set, so game.js takes the `if (netStart)` branch every frame.

confirmed.claim: broadleafFall()'s own on-track clearance guard (and the matching `ctx.note` bounding box, and canopyR's `broadleafFall` estimate used by tracks.js `plantTree`) underestimate the tree's actual rendered canopy radius by the lobe's radial offset, so a broadleaf-fall tree can be placed close enough that its foliage geometry overlaps the tarmac/barrier it was supposed to clear.
confirmed.evidence: Lines 320-325: each crown lobe is a frustum centred at point `p`, offset from the trunk axis by `rr = h * 0.16 * spread` (line 321), with the widest lobe (i=0) having `rT = h * (0.34 - 0*0.08) * spread = h*0.34*spread` (line 324-325). Since a frustum's footprint is a circle of that radius centred at `p`, the true farthest reach from the trunk axis is `rr + rT = h*0.16*spread + h*0.34*spread = h*0.50*spread`. But the guard at line 307 (`onTrack(a.c[0], a.c[2], h * 0.34 * spread + 0.8)`) and the bbox at lines 311-312 (`[h * 0.68 * spread, h, h * 0.68 * spread]`, i.e. half-width `h*0.34*spread`) both only account for `rT`, omitting the `rr` offset entirely. confirmed.fix: Account for the lobe offset in all three places: change the guard/canopyR/bbox formula to `h * 0.50 * spread + 0.8` (or compute `rr + max(rB,rT)` precisely) so placement and the on-track guard match the actual frustum footprint.

confirmed.claim: The machine-checked G contract declares `announce` with two parameters, but the real function takes a third `kind` argument that a module actually passes.
confirmed.evidence: Line 524: `readonly announce: (msg: string, dur?: number) => void;`. js/game.js:1142 is `function announce(msg, dur, kind) { kind = kind || "race"; const pri = ANN_PRI[kind] || 2; ... }` — `kind` selects the announce priority class, which decides whether a message survives a cinematic camera and whether it pre-empts a queued one. js/ui/onboard.js:54 calls `G.announce(`${verb(key)} — ${TAIL[key]}`, 2.5, "coach")`. The tsc leg cannot catch this: `emitShadow()` in tools/check/check-gctx.mjs emits reads as `void G.announce;` only, so call arity and parameter types are never checked.
confirmed.fix: Change the declaration to `readonly announce: (msg: string, dur?: number, kind?: string) => void;`.

confirmed.claim: `ReliabilityLevel` documents the wrong value set — "normal" and "high" do not exist and "real" is missing — for the enum that gates the `raceReliability` setter.

confirmed.evidence: Line 3177 is `els.pausemenu.hidden = true; els.results.hidden = true; els.announce.hidden = true;` — the only announce-related write in quitToMenu (I read the whole function, 3161-3205). confirmed.claim: `ALT_INSIDE` is documented as marking teams (specifically Cadillac) whose `alt` colour should be scored only against the mark, not the field — but the table is left permanently empty, so that branch of `markPalette`'s alt-scoring and the corresponding assertions in crest-marks.test.mjs are silently never exercised for any team, including the one the comment names.
confirmed.evidence: Lines 493-501: 'Which marks paint their alt INSIDE the mark rather than beside it. Cadillac's eight detail layers land 99.4% of their area on its crest ... so the field is a surface that alt never touches ... brand near-black failed the field test, nothing else in the pool cleared 2.4, and the grey ramp answered.' followed by `const ALT_INSIDE = {};` — a literal empty object with no `cadillac: true` entry (git log -L on that region shows it was created empty in the very first commit that added the file). At line 668, `const score = ALT_INSIDE[teamId] ? (c) => contrast(c, mark) : (c) => Math.min(contrast(c, under[0]), contrast(c, mark));` therefore always takes the field-inclusive branch for every team. Two test assertions key off the same empty lookup: tests/unit/crest-marks.test.mjs:221 (`altOnField = !LT.ALT_INSIDE[team.id]`, always true) and :561 (`if (LT.ALT_INSIDE[team.id] && isGrey(P.alt)) bad.push(...)`, condition always false, so a grey Cadillac inner-detail colour would never be flagged there).
confirmed.fix: Add `cadillac: true` (and any other team whose alt is drawn strictly inside the mark) to ALT_INSIDE, matching the documented intent, so markPalette scores its alt correctly and the crest-marks.test.mjs grey-alt guard actually runs for that team.

confirmed.claim: The repair-patch roughness modulation is scoped inside the `if (iriSurface)` block, so on WebGPU it never runs on road/terrain (where GLX and TLX both apply it) and is a no-op on the iridescent car paint it is now attached to.
confirmed.evidence: WGSL lines 1043-1051: `if (iriSurface) { ... albedo = albedo * mix(...); rough = clamp(rough + (patchM - 0.5) * 0.16 * min(detail * 4.0, 1.0), 0.04, 1.0); }`. GLSL glsl-lit.js:993 has it at top level, gated only on detail: `if (uDetail > 0.0) rough = clamp(rough + (patchM - 0.5) * 0.16 * min(uDetail * 4.0, 1.0), 0.04, 1.0);` — its comment says "Repair patches read glossier: fold the patch mask into roughness (max +-0.08) before the specular AA below widens it." tsl-lit.js:1158-1160 also has it at top level under `If(matU.detail.greaterThan(0.0))`. On a car fragment detail is 0, so `min(detail*4,1)` is 0 and the line does nothing where WGSL put it. Net: WGX tarmac loses the ±0.08 gloss variation on resurfaced patches that GLX/TLX show.
confirmed.fix: Move line 1050 out of the `if (iriSurface)` block to just before the `applyMaterial(...)` call at line 1052, gated on `if (detail > 0.0)`.

confirmed.claim: Ground mist on WebGPU samples the 4-octave sky-family `fbm` instead of the 2-octave surface-family `cloudFBM` that GLX and TLX use, so the mist breakup pattern, its noise family and its value range all differ from the other two backends.
confirmed.evidence: WGSL line 1528: `let mistAmt = mistK * band * smoothstep(0.35, 0.72, fbm(mp)) * dRamp;`. GLSL glsl-lit.js:1574: `float mist = uGroundMist * band * smoothstep(0.35, 0.72, cloudFBM(mp)) * dRamp;` and tsl-lit.js:1526 `.mul(smoothstep(0.35, 0.72, cloudFBM(mp)))`. The two functions are not the same: `fbm` (wgsl-chunks.js:38) is 4 octaves of `vnoise`/`hash2` (sky family, 127.1/311.7) with `p = p * 2.02`, summing to a max of 0.9375; `cloudFBM` (wgsl-chunks.js:615, already defined in this file and used by cloudShadow) is 2 octaves of `svnoise`/`hash21` (surface family, 123.34/456.21) with `p = p * 2.03 + 1.7`, max 0.75. Against the fixed 0.35/0.72 smoothstep band a 0.75-max signal and a 0.9375-max signal of a different hash give materially different mist coverage on every misty/dawn circuit.
confirmed.fix: Change `fbm(mp)` to `cloudFBM(mp)` on line 1528.

confirmed.claim: The WGSL sky drops the overcast damping from `coronaDamp`, so under heavy cloud the sun aureole, the tight corona ring and the sun disc all render at full strength on WebGPU instead of the ~8% GLX and TLX leave.
confirmed.evidence: WGSL line 1854: `let coronaDamp = 1.0 - nightSky;`. GLSL glsl-sky.js:318: `float coronaDamp = (1.0 - overcast * 0.92) * (1.0 - nightSky);` with the block comment at 300 ("Sun corona + disc (damped under overcast)") and at 307 ("overcast <= 1 keeps the first factor >= 0.08"). tsl-sky.js:377 carries the GLX form: `overcast.mul(0.92).oneMinus().mul(nightSky.oneMinus())`. All three consumers on WGSL lines 1856/1857/1862 (aureole, corona ring, disc) are multiplied by it, so at `overcast` 1 (cloud >= 1) WGX paints a full-brightness HDR sun disc (`discCore` up to 2.8×sunWarm) through a solid grey overcast lid.
confirmed.fix: Line 1854: `let coronaDamp = (1.0 - overcast * 0.92) * (1.0 - nightSky);`

confirmed.claim: The WGSL city-skyglow block omits GLX's cloud-belly pickup term entirely, so on night circuits the cloud deck over a lit city does not glow from below on WebGPU.
confirmed.evidence: WGSL lines 1900-1903 contain only the horizon dome: `let horiz = pow(clamp(1.0 - max(dir.y, 0.0) * 2.4, 0.0, 1.0), 3.0 * cityGlowReach); c = c + U.cityGlow.xyz * horiz;` and then the block ends. GLSL glsl-sky.js:411-417 adds, inside the same `uCityGlow` gate: `float pickup = cityCov * (0.35 + 0.65 * cityThick) * clamp(1.0 - dir.y * 1.6, 0.0, 1.0); c += uCityGlow * pickup * 0.45;` ("the cloud deck over a lit city glows from BELOW — thick bellies catch the most uplight"). tsl-sky.js:446-448 ports it. WGSL even computes `covRay` (line 1807) for star occlusion but never stores `thick` for this use, so the whole term is absent.
confirmed.fix: Hoist `thick` into a `cityThick` var alongside `covRay` at line 1807-1808 and add the two pickup lines after line 1902, matching glsl-sky.js:415-417.

confirmed.claim: The composite's midtone-contrast `pow` floors its base at 0.0 instead of the 1e-6 GLSL uses, re-opening the pow(0, n) mobile-GPU NaN the GLSL comment exists to close — on every pure-black pixel of every frame.
confirmed.evidence: WGSL line 614: `c = pow(max(c, vec3<f32>(0.0)), vec3<f32>(contrast));`. GLSL glsl-post.js:615: `c = pow(max(c, vec3(1e-6)), vec3(uContrast));   // pow(0, n) NaNs on mobile GPUs; black stays black`. The same guard is applied elsewhere in the GLSL family for the same stated reason (glsl-lit.js:1380 "base floored 1e-4: pow(0.0,exp)=NaN on mobile GPUs (log2(0)=-Inf)"; glsl-sky.js:409). WGSL `pow` is defined as `exp2(e2 * log2(e1))`, so `log2(0) = -inf` and the result is implementation-defined; a NaN here propagates through vibrance, saturation, tint and the black-lift `max` to the swapchain. Default contrast is 1.12, so the exponent is non-integral and the fast path cannot save it.
confirmed.fix: Line 614: `c = pow(max(c, vec3<f32>(1e-6)), vec3<f32>(contrast));`

confirmed.claim: The TSL composite's midtone-contrast `pow` floors its base at 0.0 instead of GLSL's 1e-6, the same dropped pow(0,n) guard as the WGSL port.
confirmed.evidence: tsl-post.js:779: `c.assign(pow(max(c, vec3(0.0)), vec3(C.contrast)));`. GLSL glsl-post.js:615: `c = pow(max(c, vec3(1e-6)), vec3(uContrast));   // pow(0, n) NaNs on mobile GPUs; black stays black`. TLX ships on both a WebGL2 and a WebGPU backend; on the WebGPU path this lowers to WGSL `pow` (exp2/log2), where log2(0) is -inf. Every black pixel (letterboxed bars, night sky, the inside of a tunnel) is a candidate.
confirmed.fix: Line 779: `pow(max(c, vec3(1e-6)), vec3(C.contrast))`.

confirmed.claim: The WGSL sky's cloud-thickness FBM drops the `evo` time-warp term, so cloud shape never evolves on WebGPU — the deck only translates.
confirmed.evidence: WGSL line 1808: `let thick = clamp(fbm(cp2 * 0.55 + vec2<f32>(3.1, 1.7)) * 2.0 - 0.55, 0.0, 1.0);`. GLSL glsl-sky.js:183 defines `float evo = cT * 0.00035;` ("Evolution: a very slow warp of the second octave to change cloud shape") and line 217 uses it: `fbm(cp2 * 0.55 + vec2(3.1 + evo, 1.7))`. tsl-sky.js:266/294 ports it (`const evo = cT.mul(0.00035)` … `vec2(evo.add(3.1), 1.7)`). The WGSL file never declares `evo` at all, so thin/thick banding across the deck is frozen relative to the drift.
confirmed.fix: Add `let evo = cT * 0.00035;` next to line 1786 and use `vec2<f32>(3.1 + evo, 1.7)` on line 1808.

confirmed.claim: The SSR grazing-self-reflection reject normalizes the hit-point cross product unguarded, so a degenerate (zero-length) basis yields a NaN normal and the reject silently fails to fire.
confirmed.evidence: wgsl-post.js:1311: `var hN = normalize(cross(hdx, hdy));` followed by `if (dot(hN, upVSn) > 0.55) { continue; }`. GLSL glsl-post.js:951-955 guards it: `vec3 hcr = cross(hdx, hdy); float hcl = length(hcr); vec3 hN = hcl > 1e-6 ? hcr / hcl : upVSn; if (hN.z < 0.0) hN = -hN; if (dot(hN, upVSn) > 0.55) continue;`. tsl-post.js:641 ports the guard (`select(hcl.greaterThan(1e-6), hcr.div(hcl), upVSn)`). With a NaN `hN`, `dot(hN, upVSn) > 0.55` is false, so the road accepts a self-hit it was meant to reject — the exact "wet mirror fills with tarmac and reads matte" case glsl-post.js:934-946 documents, at the depth-quantised grazing distances where the basis degenerates.
confirmed.fix: Replace line 1311 with the guarded form: compute `hcr = cross(hdx, hdy)`, `hcl = length(hcr)`, `var hN = select(upVSn, hcr / hcl, hcl > 1e-6);`.

confirmed.claim: The TSL screen sun-shaft loop omits the outer-reach early-out both other backends carry, so every full-res pixel beyond the shaft radius runs 8 dependent bloom taps whose result is multiplied by an exact 0.
confirmed.evidence: tsl-post.js:724: `If(dist.greaterThan(0.005), () => { ... 8-tap Loop ... const radial = clamp(dist.mul(float(2.6).div(C.shaftSpread)), 0.0, 1.0).oneMinus(); c.addAssign(shaft.mul(C.sunShaft).mul(radial).mul(radial).mul(0.60)); });`. GLSL glsl-post.js:1144 guards the same block with `if (dist > 0.005 && dist * (2.6 / uShaftSpread) < 1.0)` and its comment states the radial term "hits an EXACT 0.0 at dist = uShaftSpread/2.6 and stays there … over half of a day frame at the shipped spread". wgsl-post.js:814 carries the identical guard. At the shipped spread 1.0 the live disc is pi*0.3846² ≈ 46% of the frame, so the majority of full-res pixels pay 8 dependent texture fetches for nothing on every sunlit frame.
confirmed.fix: Add `.and(dist.mul(float(2.6).div(max(C.shaftSpread, 1e-3))).lessThan(1.0))` to the `If` condition on line 724.

confirmed.claim: `poolUsed` in tlx.js is write-only: incremented once per acquired mesh wrapper every frame and reset in four places, but never read anywhere.
confirmed.evidence: Read tlx.js:1467 (`let poolUsed = 0; // acquired THIS batch — diagnostics only, never an index`), the single increment at tlx.js:1826 inside acquireMesh, and the four resets at tlx.js:2620, 2631, 2698 and 3098. Grepped `\bpoolUsed\b` across js/, tools/ and tests/: the only other hits are comments in tlx.js and assertions in tests/unit/gfx-backend-canary.test.mjs:3611-3636, which only assert that `meshPool[poolUsed]` and `for (let i = poolUsed; ...)` do NOT appear (and note at line 3624 that "poolUsed may survive as a counter"). __tlx.memState() (tlx.js:3606) reports `pool: meshPool.length`, `draws`, `geoKeys` and `batch` — not poolUsed. No consumer exists.
confirmed.fix: Delete the declaration at tlx.js:1467, the increment at 1826 and the four `poolUsed = 0;` resets, keeping the `_poolBatch++` bumps.

confirmed.claim: `_softBlitGen = seq` in _softBlitNotify is a dead write — the only read of _softBlitGen sits on a branch that can never observe a value other than the initial 0.
confirmed.evidence: Read wgx.js:2140-2143: `_softBlitShown = seq; _softBlitGen = seq;`. Grepped `_softBlitGen` in wgx.js: declared at 670 (`let _softBlitGen = 0`), written only here, and read only at wgx.js:2181 — `if (!_softGpu || !_displayCtx) return Promise.resolve(_softBlitGen);` inside awaitSoftPresent. _softBlitNotify is reached only from _softDisplayFinish's map callback (wgx.js:2111), which requires `_displayCtx` truthy, and _softDisplayEncode (wgx.js:2052) requires `_softGpu && _displayCtx`; _displayCtx is only ever assigned on the _softGpu path (wgx.js:5965) and a failure there returns _bootFail. So the read at 2181 is taken only when soft-present is off, i.e. when nothing has ever written the variable. softPresentState() (wgx.js:2170-2177) reports `seq`/`shown`, not this. Every consumer of the blit generation uses _softBlitShown / _softSceneGen instead.
confirmed.fix: Delete `_softBlitGen = seq;` at wgx.js:2142 and return `_softBlitShown` (or a plain 0) from the awaitSoftPresent early-out at 2181.

confirmed.claim: Three narrow/compact-viewport overrides of #pc-toggle in tuner.css can never take visual effect because hud.css's unconditional #pc-toggle rule lives in a higher-precedence cascade layer.
confirmed.evidence: tokens.css:13 declares `@layer reset, base, components, hud, overlays;` (hud outranks components regardless of specificity or matched media/container conditions). tuner.css wraps its whole file in `@layer components` (tuner.css:1) and, inside that layer, sets `@container sheet (max-width: 220px) { #pc-toggle { width: 100%; min-width: 0; } }` at tuner.css:899-901, plus `:is(#lighting-inner, #camtune-inner)[data-density="compact"] #pc-toggle { padding: 6px 10px; font-size: var(--fs-micro); }` at tuner.css:612 and a third padding/min-height override at tuner.css:704-707 for the compact+rail-off state. hud.css wraps its whole file in `@layer hud` (hud.css:1) and unconditionally sets `#pc-toggle { width: auto; ...; padding: calc(var(--gap) * 0.75) calc(var(--gap) * 7 / 6); font-size: var(--fs-micro); ... }` at hud.css:933-940 with no @layer override of its own. Per the CSS cascade, layer order is checked before specificity/source order, so hud.css's width/padding for #pc-toggle always wins over all three tuner.css overrides even when their container/attribute conditions match. Grepped `#pc-toggle` across all 11 css files (only hud.css and tuner.css define it) and confirmed hud.css has no matching @layer components block that would neutralize the mismatch.
confirmed.fix: Move the #pc-toggle base rule into @layer components (or move tuner.css's #pc-toggle overrides into @layer hud) so the narrow/compact overrides can actually win over the base rule.
